messages:
maria: Quick thread — putting together a benchmark narrative that ties latency to unit economics for launch. need a fast gut-check on two chart directions + what copy/messaging avoids pricing confusion. rough plan below.

alex: can you paste the sample numbers you used? i'll run a quick normalization so we can compare apples-to-apples.

maria: simple sketch first — option A is an axis chart (median latency ms vs $/1k tokens). option B is a 'tokens per $' ranked bar with a small 95th-tail inset. numbers (toy):
```
model,median_latency_ms,cost_per_1k,tokens_per_$
Redwood-XL,120,0.12,8333
OpenLite-2,250,0.05,20000
FP16-Pegg,180,0.08,12500
```

jordan: i lean toward option B (tokens-per-$) for the landing hero — more intuitive for buyers who think in cost/throughput. option A could work in a deeper-dive section.

sam: agree with jordan on hero. also: emphasize predictable latency (p95/p99) not just median — enterprise buyers care about tail/SLAs. avoid language like "fastest" unless we can back it with p95.

casey: for inbound routing, split CTAs: PLG dev -> self-serve trial + quickstart; Platform/SRE -> request demo/architecture call. we'll need two short snippets for ad copy and the webinar CTA.

alex: note on the numbers — those cost per 1k tokens are synthetic. recommend showing percentage deltas or normalized index (Redwood=1.0) to avoid public pricelist assumptions. we can include a footnote: "based on test workload X, see data appendix."

maria: good call. alternative hero copy lines: "More predictable token economics at scale" or "Cut inference $/latency for production workloads." which reads better?

jordan: first one — "predictable token economics" signals ops/control. second is more headline-y for webinars.

casey: for webinar hook i'd use the second one but tighten: "How we cut inference $/latency for production apps." 30s teaser script: 1) problem (spiky costs, tail latency), 2) what we did (batching + routing + model profiles), 3) result (lower $/token, stable p95).

maria: action items: alex -> normalized delta chart + p95 inset (due Thu EOD), jordan -> two hero mockups (tokens-per-$ vs axis) by Fri AM, casey -> routing copy + webinar 30s by Fri. sam -> polish the p95 framing and a one-paragraph data appendix.

alex: flagged — i'll also add a short note about batching/kv-cache effects so we don't oversell raw model numbers.

deploy-bot: Shortcut created: https://app.shortcut.com/redwood-inference/story/bench-ops-1768904322 (assigned: alex, jordan, casey, sam)

maria: sweet. one more ask — let's make the landing charts downloadable (png + CSV) so prospects can eyeball numbers. keeps the messaging transparent.

casey: 👍 i'll wire the routing flows into the marketing automation: PLG signup gets tokenized follow-up content; enterprise demo route triggers AE alert + product qualification form.

jordan: mockups will include a compact explainer tooltip for "tokens per $" and a tiny legend for p95 inset. avoids cognitive load.

maria: perfect. reconvene Tue standup to review drafts. thanks all :thumbsup:
